# Organised industrial research laboratory (`industrial_research_lab`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/institutions.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Institutions, law & governance (`institutions`)
- Deps: needs scientific_method; helped by patents, university, systematic_invention, joint_stock_company
- Core idea: A firm or state employs trained scientists and craftsmen full time, in one building with shared instruments and workshops, to work on problems chosen for their value to the enterprise. Invention becomes a planned, budgeted activity instead of the luck of a lone genius. What makes it work: a mix of theorists, experimenters and model-makers in daily contact, a steady income that tolerates projects lasting years, laboratory notebooks signed and dated, patents to capture results, and a clear path from laboratory to factory.
- Pitfalls:
  - Expecting results in months: Bell Labs' solid-state work ran for a decade before the transistor
  - Hiring scientists but keeping them apart from the workshops and from the people who know the practical problems
  - Directing every step from above, or the opposite, leaving researchers with no problem that matters to anyone
  - Crediting Edison alone with the idea: German dye firms and university teaching laboratories set the pattern
- History: china: Song to Qing – state workshops and bureaus (arsenals, porcelain, the astronomical bureau) concentrate skilled staff on set tasks, without experimental research as a goal; islamic: 1259 – Maragha observatory: a funded staff, instruments and library on a long programme; europe: 1576 – Tycho Brahe's Uraniborg, a staffed research establishment; 1826 Liebig's teaching laboratory at Giessen; 1870s–1880s in-house laboratories at BASF, Hoechst and Bayer; 1887 Physikalisch-Technische Reichsanstalt, Berlin; americas: 1876 – Edison's Menlo Park 'invention factory'; 1900 General Electric Research Laboratory; 1925 Bell Telephone Laboratories; east_asia: 1917 – RIKEN founded in Japan
- Read:
  - Jon Gertner, The Idea Factory: Bell Labs and the Great Age of American Innovation (2012)
  - Leonard S. Reich, The Making of American Industrial Research: Science and Business at GE and Bell, 1876–1926 (1985)
